blocks.p: Rei went home on the first train of the morning, with the registry copied into the back of Gin's book in his own bad handwriting. The sky over Iidabashi was turning grey, and the crows were already loud on the wires. The first Namboku train north was nearly empty. A cleaner in a blue uniform dozed at one end of the carriage with her mop bucket between her knees. A young couple in festival clothes, a cotton yukata each, sat holding hands with their eyes shut, still wearing the paper wristbands from some party the night before. Nobody spoke. The train ran under the sleeping city, and Rei sat with the book on his knees and did not open it until he was home.

Higuchi had said that Gin copied the names too. So Rei went looking, and he found them. They were in a section near the end of the book that he had only skimmed in the first week, when they had read like notes about strangers. There was a page headed The Thirteen. There was a page of rank letters. And there were thirteen short files, one for each domain, full of the small practical details Gin always wrote down. Where to go. When. Who in the city already knew. With the ledger beside him, the strangers became people. Rei read them at the kitchen table while the kettle ticked as it cooled.

doc.title: The holders. In my words (G.U.)
lines: The thirteen are people. Former practitioners. Former Guardian rank practitioners who crossed a threshold the taxonomy has no category for, whose aperture expanded to the point where they could take one of the Font's thirteen structural domains and hold it. One emotional register of the veil's membrane. Permanently. For as long as the membrane needs holding.

They are not divine. They are not in thrones. They are walking around in ordinary cities, eating ordinary meals, carrying something vast by will alone. Some of them have been doing this for centuries. Some are newer. All of them are tired in the specific way of someone who cannot stop.

They are not the strongest practitioners alive. They are people who found a way to be in relationship with the Axis without disappearing into it. They present to it as a function rather than a person. The domain is larger than any one person, and so it survives being that close.
The Axis cannot hold the emotional layer itself. It is no longer human enough to hold emotions as shapes with weight and centre. The holders can.

They find each other. Not through institutions. Through the recognition that happens when two people carrying the same structural weight meet. The network is real. It has no name. It has no schedule. It meets irregularly. It is the only structure in the world that knows the veil is thinning from the inside, and that the thirteen are the reason it has not already failed.

blocks.p: Next to it, Gin had copied the top two lines of the CVD's rank chart. The CVD ranks every practitioner with a letter, from E at the bottom up through D, C, B, A and S. Above those sit two ranks almost nobody ever sees written down.

doc.title: Rank chart. The top two lines, copied from the CVD sheet
lines: SS. Singularity. Foundational pillars. Known only to CVD leadership. Secret candidates for the Thirteen if a Guardian falls.
SSS. Guardian. The Thirteen. Supreme protectors of veil stability. Aligned with specific emotions. Their existence is not public knowledge.
Every holder file I have found lists the rank as Guardian.

blocks.p: Then came the thirteen files. Gin had written each one the same way. First the holder, with their age, their work, their path, and the weight they carried. Then, under Who knows, the ordinary people in the city who had noticed something about that holder without being told.

blocks.cap: Asakura Mio, the first of the Thirteen, who holds Grief

doc.title: The Thirteen. Who, where, and who already knows (G.U.)
lines: I. GRIEF. Asakura Mio, 27. Barista at a tea house in Kyoto. Regular hours. Clairsentience. Dark circles since she was twenty-three. She does not hide them. Whoever sits near her finds whatever they are grieving rising to the surface. She cannot turn this off and stopped trying. She was identified at seventeen and prepared until twenty-two. In March 2011 the largest grief event in modern Japanese memory hit the membrane before succession was ready, and Domain I has been on emergency stabilisation ever since. The CVD does not know. To find her, go to the right tea house three evenings in a row. She will know you were there before you introduce yourself.

Who knows. Hino Miho, 28, Kabukichō. Self-taught, Arbiter-rank Clairsentience, nine years of managing the worst ground in Tokyo alone with no instruction. She has a read on the hotel room where something happened to Domain I in 2011. She has been waiting three years for someone to ask her about it. My notes on her run to thirty-eight pages.

II. RAGE. Mori Takao, 48. Held since he was twenty-eight. Twenty years. The eldest of the Thirteen, and the one the others defer to. Telekinesis. Listed in the CVD system as a retired field operative. He is not retired. He tends the boiler of a public bath in Kita. Rage carries the highest entity pressure in Tokyo, and it produces the most aggressive crossing attempts of any domain. Something on the other side circles his seat. Hard to find, on purpose. Go to the places people go when they have nowhere left to go.
Who knows. Old Tomi, the last man living in the condemned blocks by the freight yard. He sits at his window at night and counts what comes through the fence. He has seen Mori cross.

III. LOVE. Sakuma Kei, 31. Gold wire glasses. Runs a small family mediation practice with a three-year waiting list. His clients do not know why they feel so completely heard. Clairsentience. He can name the exact nature of any bond in front of him. The most stable domain of the thirteen. He calls it maintenance. It is the hardest kind, keeping something good from turning into something else.
Who knows. Kawai Yuki, 57, Akebono Bakery by the station. Up at four. Kei is the dawn regular she feeds.

IV. FEAR. Nakashima Yuna, 40. Director of a security consultancy. Psychometabolism. She can steady a practitioner in crisis in under thirty seconds. For twelve years she has been building a taxonomy of what the fear domain actually produces. Not all of it is hostile. Some of it is warning systems older than the Accord. The CVD uses her taxonomy without credit. She has noticed. She files nothing and does everything. Her calendar is public. Her assistant knows more than most practitioners.
Who knows. The Woman at the Back, the Suzuran, two in the morning, every night. She feels Yuna coming. Kubo, the blind busker in the station underpass, hears her pass.

V. WONDER. Chen Lian, 29, from Chengdu, came to Japan at eighteen. Identified at twenty-one. Eight years in the seat. Researcher at the Grid Archive, with pre-Accord documents no institution holds. The Grid's pre-Accord oral archive opens through her. Clairsentience. She can read the history of a room from the street outside. The only domain whose presence actively helps practitioners. Wonder produces clarity.
Who knows. Master Lin Wei at the Taoist temple. He respects her. Buy incense before you ask him anything.

VI. DESPAIR. Watanabe Jun, 35. Looks older. Telepathy. He can read the despair of a place without touching it, and he spots practitioners heading into a crash before they know. He has tried to retire three times. There is no mechanism for it. He finds that, specifically, accurate. He says despair, handled correctly, is the emotion that sees reality most clearly. Either wisdom or a symptom. He says it is both. Reach him through the Grid's emergency network.
Who knows. Okuma Sumi, who tends the riverside memorial at dusk. She felt him at the water.

VII. JOY. Hoshino Haru, 33. Noodle shop on Sakae Street, Kita. The broth takes eight hours. Psychometabolism. His teacher held Joy for forty years and prepared him for twelve. The cleanest succession on record. Haru spent three years wondering if he was doing it wrong because it had not been difficult. He was not doing it wrong. The quality of the food and the quality of the domain are the same thing.
Who knows. Maruyama at Café Mikazuki. Tatsu at the Tatsuya counter under the tracks. Haru is a warm regular to both.

VIII. SHAME. Kobayashi Emi, 36. Institutional accountability work. Telepathy. Shame entities chase something that looks like justice from one angle. She has been negotiating with them for twelve years. She is very good at it. She does not enjoy it, which is probably why she is good at it.
Who knows. Father Anselm Mabuchi, the parish house beside the church near our building. He hears her confession.

IX. HUNGER. Inoue Satoru, 36. No fixed location. Teleportation. The last holder died three years ago and the seat went vacant. He was an emergency succession, found and installed in months instead of years. He knows the gaps. He is managing them. This is the domain the organised entity campaign is pushing hardest. Reach him only through the Grid's emergency protocols.

X. COURAGE. Okabe Natsumi, 42. Independent. Complicated relationship with the CVD. Psychometabolism. Keeps field notes she shares only with practitioners who prove they can use them. Linked to Domain IV. Fear is anticipation. Courage is going forward anyway. She and Yuna have worked in step for twelve years. The first five were difficult.

XI. LONGING. Park Junho, 41, born in Seoul, seventeen years in Tokyo. Teaches Korean at the community centre in Shin-Ōkubo, Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Clairsentience. He knows when someone is missing someone before they say it. Longing entities are not dangerous. They just do not let go. He has worked with them for fifteen years. He finds them heartbreaking. He does not find that a problem.
Who knows. Pak Sun-ja, the mudang, in the shrine room behind the curtain above the Korean restaurant. She keeps his secret.

XII. AWE. Kasumi Shin, 39. Variable. The closest of the thirteen to the Axis. Instruments give no consistent reading on him. He arrived at a very old place very young and has managed that closeness for fifteen years. He has the Account Book. He showed it to me. Go to him with something real. He has not been fooled about what is real in fifteen years. Pre-Accord documents, the Grid's full oral archive, the oldest intelligence network still working.
Who knows. Miyamoto Kazuo, kannushi at the shrine. He knows when Kasumi visits.
XIII. DUTY. Vacant since 2009. Kita district. The Axis carries it directly. Not sustainable.

blocks.p: One name in the files Rei had to stop on. Kabukichō is the night district of Shinjuku, all bars, hosts and neon, open until dawn. Gin had called it the worst ground in Tokyo, and Rei believed him.

doc.title: Stuck beside VII
lines: I know who he is. I recommend the broth anyway.

doc.title: On XIII (G.U.)
lines: The CVD files the thirteenth register as null-emotive. Their instruments were built to measure emotion by how much it moves. XIII does not move. The instruments read the stillness as absence.
I think that is wrong. I cannot yet say what is right. Something is in that seat's register, and it is not nothing. Keys on the hook.

blocks.p: Rei read the last line three times. Then he turned back to the sixth file. He put his finger on the name with two stars beside it in the ledger, and on the word Itabashi that Higuchi had pencilled next to it. Itabashi was the ward just west of Kita, close enough to walk. Rei did not sleep.
